headline: Medium risk: shared file-based workflows can leak or corrupt documents, while Opik’s broad egress and Unstructured’s write/subprocess defaults create downstream and conflict hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Opik has broad network egress and REST API I/O, while Unstructured reads and writes files and supports subprocesses. If Opik ingests Unstructured-produced text from a shared workspace or API payload, attacker-controlled document content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Opik consumes Unstructured output from a shared file or API field without provenance tags, injection is plausible.
IF Unstructured processes attacker-supplied documents that Opik later parses as instructions, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance header to all handoffs.
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like text before enabling automation.
Disable automatic execution of any text extracted from documents.
Use separate workspaces for raw documents and agent prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured explicitly reads and writes filesystem documents, and Opik has broad network egress. If both touch the same workspace, document contents can flow from Unstructured into Opik and then out over the network. No secret-handling or isolation controls are documented here, so the shared-workspace leakage path is credible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, document contents can be exposed to Opik.
IF Opik forwards workspace text to external services, leakage extends beyond the local host.
mitigations: Keep raw documents in a separate directory from Opik inputs.
Restrict Opik to non-sensitive test data for initial runs.
Turn off any automatic upload or telemetry paths in Opik.
Use a one-way export file that strips sensitive fields first.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with container mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured can read/write files, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; it also supports multiple instances. Opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared artifacts, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible. The profiles do not show locking, so the conflict risk is more than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Unstructured runs multiple instances against shared artifacts, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent its own output directory.
Run only one Unstructured instance per workspace.
Check for existing files before writing new outputs.
Pause Opik writes while Unstructured is mutating files.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured produces document/text outputs that Opik can ingest through REST/API workflows. If Opik treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into downstream evaluation or reporting. The pair has no documented validation step, so the default path is an unverified handoff rather than a checked one.
conditions: IF Opik consumes Unstructured extractions without a validation step, errors can propagate.
IF extracted text is used as ground truth in downstream reports, the cascade becomes material.
mitigations: Add a human review step for extracted fields.
Compare a small sample against source documents before automation.
Reject outputs that lack source offsets or confidence markers.
Limit downstream use to draft-only workflows.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for extracted records.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU residency, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent. Opik is open-source with broad egress, and Unstructured documents privacy-policy and docs URLs, but the profiles do not show a concrete residency or retention conflict. Because the evidence is sparse, I keep this low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Opik to external services, a compliance review is needed.
IF Unstructured is configured to process restricted documents, retention policy alignment must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in initial pair runs.
Review the privacy policy links before production use.
Document where outputs are stored and for how long.
Confirm both tools are covered by the same data-processing terms.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the pipeline.
